![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Avoid using order-sensitive array comparisons like `toEqual` when the order of elements (such as SQL grant targets parsed from a file) is not guaranteed or semantically significant. Instead, use order-insensitive assertions, such as verifying the array length and checking element presence with `toContain` or set-based checks.

```javascript
    expect(grantTargets).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(grantTargets).toContain('rubric_points');
    expect(grantTargets).toContain('rubric_points_ready_v1');
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid using JSON.stringify for array comparisons in tests because it is strictly order-sensitive. Instead, use order-insensitive assertions, such as verifying the array length and checking element presence with includes or set-based checks.
</details>

Addressed in b8547537a: the service-role grant target assertion now checks the expected count and membership independently of statement order. Verified with the focused static contract suite (16/16), ESLint, and git diff --check.
